name: morph-slider

frames.best_why: A settled mountain photo with caption, arrows and dots all visible and no cursor over the slide.

tagline: Photos melt into each other inside a rounded slider with arrows and dots.
summary: A full-width image slider whose slides dissolve through a liquid melt, ripple, shear or swirl effect. Captions cross-fade, arrows step through slides and dots mark the position.
appearance: A large rounded rectangle holding a full-bleed landscape photo, framed by a thin black border of empty stage. A dark translucent caption sits at the bottom left, round arrow buttons at mid height and a row of small dots at the bottom centre.
behaviour: Slides change with a shader that warps and melts the outgoing photo into the incoming one, briefly smearing colours. Captions fade and lift, the active dot stretches, and autoplay advances after a pause while hovering stops it.
demo_content: Captions Dolomites at first light, Coastline late afternoon, Desert road golden hour, over mountain and building photos.
search_phrases: draggable photo carousel with melt effect
use_when: A hero or gallery wants a cinematic photo carousel with a stand-out transition and captions.
avoid_when: The morph is a WebGL shader, so it is heavy on low-end devices and needs a fixed-height, sized parent.
customise: Items, start index, transition mode, duration, easing, intensity, scale, aberration, drift, autoplay and delay, loop, radius, overlay colour, captions, controls and indicators are props.
weight_why: A WebGL shader plus a continuous requestAnimationFrame render loop for the drift.

a11y.note: Captions use a live region and controls are labelled; reduced motion only shortens the morph instead of removing it.

issues: Captions do not match the photos shown: the desert-road caption sits over a green alpine valley.
polish_why: Cinematic slides and clean controls, but the caption and photo mismatch is noticeable.
